gen-mystery-quest-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Mystery Quest feels bookish and a little nostalgic. Noto Sans Lepcha, a sans-serif with the stature of cast iron capitals and curves that keep a wide opening, gives the pair its sturdy, approachable footing.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Noto Mandaic reads tall and curvy. Its lowercase rises close to capitals, so Mystery Quest, with open jaws on every curve and compact ascenders, can carry the nostalgic storybook mood above it.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-noto-sans-meroitic: Bookish, a bit wistful, and see-through. Noto Sans Meroitic fills the line like capitals, while Mystery Quest does its best work as the nostalgic display voice with open jaws on its curves.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-noto-sans-multani: Nostalgic charm comes from Mystery Quest, whose open jaws and compact ascenders sit above a body with a lofty x-height. Noto Sans Multani, a modern sans-serif, keeps its e wide open below.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Noto Sans Nabataean reads almost cap-tall, with wide-open s curves. Mystery Quest is best at bookish, nostalgic display, with open jaws and compact ascenders, while the sans-serif below does the contemporary, professional work.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-noto-sans-old-hunga: Big, friendly counters and a bookish wink. Mystery Quest brings nostalgia with its open-jawed curves, and Noto Sans Old Hungarian keeps its tall a, e and s apertures open even at tiny sizes.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-noto-sans-old-persi: Nostalgic from the first curve, Mystery Quest earns its keep set big and short. Noto Sans Old Persian, a lofty sans-serif, lets its open counters breathe underneath.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-noto-sans-old-turki: Storybook curves with open jaws and compact ascenders lead, while Noto Sans Old Turkic follows as a chunky, tall sans-serif that stays clear. Bookish up top, approachable below.
